title: Bradley-Terry Rankings for Recommender Systems Across Dataset Taxonomies

problem.claim: Ranking recommendation algorithms is challenging because performance is sensitive to dataset characteristics.

gap.claim: Naive aggregation of benchmark performance metrics can produce misleading rankings and undermine practical algorithm selection.

contributions.claim: A data-driven recommendation-algorithm ranking methodology based on the Bradley-Terry model.
A metric for evaluating ranking consistency and a robustness approach for incomplete data.
A dataset-specific methodology for ranking algorithms on unseen datasets without running the models, using Bradley-Terry extensions including BT trees and covariate-based BT models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the data-driven Bradley-Terry ranking methodology and the ranking-consistency metric as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The obtained ranking depends on key dataset statistics.
The authors report robustness of their ranking to incomplete data.
The proposed unseen-dataset methodology ranks algorithms without running the models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Algorithm rankings are sensitive to dataset characteristics.
A fair comparison methodology is needed because naive metric aggregation can mislead rankings.
The paper introduces a Bradley-Terry-based data-driven ranking methodology.
Rankings depend on dataset statistics, with reported consistency evaluation and robustness to incomplete data.
Bradley-Terry extensions support dataset-specific ranking on unseen datasets without model execution.

source_observation.claim: Algorithm rankings depend on dataset statistics.

interpretation.claim: Benchmark comparisons should account for dataset context rather than rely only on aggregate scores.

application.claim: Use dataset-aware ranking analyses when selecting recommender algorithms across heterogeneous benchmarks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which dataset statistics are most predictive or when context-aware ranking changes a selection decision.

source_observation.claim: The proposed ranking is reported as robust to incomplete data.

interpretation.claim: Ranking methods may remain useful when benchmark results are partially missing.

application.claim: Consider incomplete-data-aware ranking when benchmark coverage is uneven.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the missing-data patterns, robustness thresholds, or evaluation conditions.

unknowns: No datasets, algorithms, or benchmark results are specified.
No numerical findings or comparison baselines are reported.
The abstract does not define the ranking-consistency metric.
The abstract does not describe the covariates, BT-tree construction, or validation conditions.
